title: Ledger
description: A royalty statement you edit in place — Tab and the arrow keys walk the grid, every cell saves itself behind a sweeping hairline, and the payout and the grand total roll digit by digit when it lands. One save fails on purpose, one row is already paid and locked, and a countdown ring gives you six seconds to take any of it back.
intent: A dense, tabular-numeral data surface on the light ground with one mechanic finished to the edge — real content, full keyboard control, and numbers that roll rather than jump, which is the interface work Herb asked for over abstract demos.

**The five fixes**

1. **Loading was a lie about the layout** — eight 68px full-width shimmer bars became seven column-shaped bars per row at the exact `--iet-row-h` (46px), so the panel no longer jerks its height and the columns no longer rewrite themselves when data lands.
2. **Status swapped instantly and grew the row** — Ready/Saving/Saved/Retry/Paid now live in a fixed-height 28px stack, each with a paired blur focus-pull enter (200ms) and a faster same-direction exit (100ms); the checkmark draws on a transition so it re-runs every save, and the failed row no longer stands 4px taller than its neighbours.
3. **Escape dropped focus to `<body>`** — cancel now returns focus to the cell you left, so the keyboard path survives a mistake; blur-cancel deliberately does not steal focus back from whatever you clicked.
4. **The grand total ignored the filter and never moved** — the footer sums the visible rows and rolls digit by digit as you type, slots are keyed from the right so adding a digit rolls instead of remapping, and a commit tints the row payout and the total green or red by direction.
